Scope checked for Turkish wording: the Mendeley deposit (five .rar archives; CFAClinic.sav has no item labels, Diagram.docx has no text) and the paper plus both ESM supplements (ESM1 = Tables 1-4, ESM2 = loading figures). Only Table 2 prints Turkish, for six items. Items i01-i05 and i11: item_text = Table 2 Turkish verbatim (no final period on items 1 and 4, as printed; item 3's 'bakış acısı' kept as printed, not corrected to 'açısı'); item_text_translated = the paper's own English column of Table 2 (study_supplied; identical to Neff's official wording). Items i06-i10 and i12: Turkish unpublished, so item_text = Neff's official SCS-SF English verbatim (official_instrument_english; item 8 has no final period in Neff's PDF, kept; item 10's line wrap joined), item_text_translated empty. instructions = Neff's English instruction block from the SCS-SF form (the study published no instructions in either language), instructions_translated empty. Hence text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=mixed. OPTIONS: the paper states '1 = almost never to 5 = almost always' in English only and Turkish anchors are not published, so option_text carries Neff's English endpoints ('Almost never'/'Almost always'; points 2-4 unlabelled on Neff's form, left blank), option_text_translated empty. DIRECTION OVERRIDE: the negatively worded items 1,4,8,9,11,12 are stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED -- every one of the 30 cross-class item correlations averages +0.160 (raw SCS compassionate vs uncompassionate items correlate negatively), each negative item correlates more with its own class (0.191-0.340) than with the positive items (0.076-0.255), and the authors' Mplus 6-factor output gives positive factor correlations across components (judgement WITH kind +0.705, over WITH kind +0.678). So on those six items resp 1 = 'Almost always' and resp 5 = 'Almost never' (anchors flipped to match the data, burkert_2019_whoqol_bref precedent); positive items keep 1 = 'Almost never', 5 = 'Almost always'. The paper never says the deposit is reverse-scored; this is inferred from the data. Step 3b clean: 12 items on 1-5 with six two-item subscales matching SCS-SF; table description names the SCS-SF clinical sample (n=246, matches Table 1). CODE DERIVATION: data/scs_2025.R pivots MIUSATR.sav columns matching ^SCS\d{2}$ by name (pattern 1: code IS the source column name). The .sav's variable labels ('SCS-SF01'..'SCS-SF12') give only the SCS-SF item NUMBER, not text, so mapping_basis is paper_explicit: codes are numbered as the canonical SCS-SF, the paper's Table 2 prints items 1,2,3,4,5,11 under those numbers with wording identical to Neff's PDF, and the deposit's own Mplus syntax assigns facets by exactly the canonical scoring key (2,6 / 11,12 / 5,10 / 4,8 / 3,7 / 1,9). Items 6-10 and 12 rely on the canonical numbering alone. TEXT: canonical English SCS-SF from Neff's PDF, verbatim incl. curly apostrophes and item 8's missing final period; item 10's PDF line wrap joined. Paper does not print the study's instructions; the PDF's instruction sentence shipped (its heading 'HOW I TYPICALLY ACT TOWARDS MYSELF IN DIFFICULT TIMES' omitted). Anchors: only endpoints labelled (1 Almost never, 5 Almost always, per PDF and paper '1 = almost never to 5 = almost always'); resp 2-4 blank. REVERSE-SCORING (overrides the instrument's printed anchors for 6 items): the negatively worded items 1,4,8,9,11,12 are stored ALREADY REVERSED in the deposit, so their option_text is flipped (1 = Almost always ... 5 = Almost never). Evidence, both halves: (a) every inter-item correlation is positive (between-polarity-block mean r = 0.17 pooled, 0.32 USA-only; min 0.001), impossible for raw SCS-SF where the positive and negative components correlate negatively; (b) this table's 545 TR rows are the deposit's non-clinical file CFANonClinic.sav (item means identical to 5 d.p.), and the deposit's psychiatric clinical sample CFAClinic.sav (n=246) scores LOWER on every positively worded item (-0.40 to -0.92) and on 11/12 items overall (total 33 vs 38), so high stored values = more self-compassion -> the positive items are raw and the negative ones reversed. Not a data defect: the storage is internally consistent; data/scs_2025.R does no recoding. VERIFICATION: verify_scs_2025_cfausatr.R PASS; PARTIAL -- pins polarity class for all 12 (each item's mean r with own polarity block exceeds the other: e.g. SCS08 0.32 vs 0.06, SCS10 0.31 vs 0.09) and storage direction; facet-pair structure is weak (mapping_structure.R 8/12, facet mate is top partner for 6/12) because 2-item SCS-SF facets within a polarity block are near-collinear; does not separate items within a facet pair or within a polarity block beyond that. LANGUAGE: English; Turkish. 545 of 670 respondents (TR) answered the authors' Turkish adaptation; the deposit (.sav/.dat/.inp/.out/Syntax.docx) carries no Turkish item text and the paper/ESM1 prints Turkish for only 6 of 12 items, so base fields hold the English (administered wording for the 125 USA respondents, collected online via the ACBS mailing list), no _translated columns, per the szameitat_2015_* multi-language ruling.
